case.question: Give us a 30-day launch marketing plan for each city: Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
expected: Proposed metrics rather than promised results

answer.headline: Two 30-day launch plans: Dubai (wider delivery-led, aggregator + social) and Abu Dhabi (tighter, community + aggregator, Khalidiya/Al Zahiyah/Khalifa City clusters), both built around observed branch formats and delivery-tooling; no verified traffic or CAC data exists, so treat all targets as test-t

items.text: Both cities: script thin outbound (rata outbound) routine: dusk calls key numbers, door-drop simple order cards, and register on aggregators with pickup enabled. Deliveroo UAE merchant tooling covers platform-rider or own-rider Marketplace+ delivery, single-order tracking, and promotional levers, but eligibility, commission and radius at a specific address are unverified.

Prepare sealed, hot/cold-separated packaging and insulated transport secondary units. Dubai Municipality delivery guidance (DM-FSD-GU63 v2, issued 2023-08-31, flagged needs_review) specifies sealed containers and separation of hot and cold items; verify current version and whether it applies to your channels before launch.

Set one shared menu architecture for both cities (anchor meaty pizza, kebab sandwiches, one family/bundled meal) so launch content is reusable; price each city separately after local cost, commission and packaging inputs. Verify by inspecting menu pages cited below (snippets are leads, not verified prices).

Days 1-7: seed content shoots at one Dubai site and list on aggregators with pickup enabled; run small geo-targeted social for your own borough-level test area, not the whole emirate. Competitor format references in Dubai include pizza branches at Al Ghurair Centre, Deira City Centre, Al Barsha Mall and Marina Diamond, plus Allo Beirut Hessa Street (advertised delivery to 4 AM) and JBR.

Days 8-21: run a limited offer through aggregator promotional levers (free delivery or buy-one-get-one style offers are described by Deliveroo UAE); fund only one offer at a time and measure contribution per order, since promotion funding, eligibility and discount cost are unverified.

Days 22-30: push repeat capture - WhatsApp/Instagram follow-up to first-order customers, a Google Maps listing check, and a mystery-shop of your own packaging and delivery time by channel. One-off
media

Differentiate on Jordanian identity and meat-forward pizza/kebab against the broad-lebanese and global-pizza formats above; the branch listings only show these formats exist at those addresses - they do not establish demand, share or absence of other cuisine.

Days 1-7: prepare in the same manner as Dubai (aggregator sign-up, packaging, photography) but concentrate door-drop and outbound work on one cluster only. Relevant competitor formats are listed around Abu Dhabi Mall/Al Zahiyah, ADNOC 913 Khalidiya, Al Wahda Mall/Al Manhal, Al Najda/Al Danah and Khalifa City (advertised hours 8 AM-12:30 AM). Proximity does not establish a shared delivery catchment; verify each address separately.

Days 8-21: run the same limited aggregator offer test as Dubai, one lever at a time, and add one local-office or community trial drop within the chosen cluster. Treat advertised competitor hours (e.g., Khalifa City to 12:30 AM, Dubai Hessa to 4 AM) as leads to test, not as evidence of demand in your trade area.

Days 22-30: verify review flow - Google Maps, aggregator replies, and a first-month promo teardown per city. Keep the Abu Dhabi and Dubai plans as separate experiments; a result in one cluster should not be assumed to transfer to another district or city.

Marketing research for this question returned no curated marketing records; the social/aggregator leads above are uninspected snippets from a single city-specific search and should be read on the original pages before you rely on them. No verified footfall, demand, cost-per-acquisition, commission or promotion-uptake data exists here.

Define launch metrics in advance (orders per day per channel, average order value, delivery share, repeat rate) and review weekly; without your cost and price inputs, no break-even or contribution figures are calculated here.

assumptions: The business is a Jordanian restaurant serving meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, planning expansion into Dubai and Abu Dhabi (from provided profile).
